provenance.gatheredBy: load-sport-data, the 2025 NCAA Division I men's and women's singles championships as played (the 2025-26 championships' singles, held in the fall of 2025 at the USTA National Campus, Orlando): each 64-player draw, its 16 national seeds and every match's winner and sets from Wikipedia's championship pages, cross-checked against the NCAA's printed brackets, which agree on every draw position, seed, winner and set score (126 matches). The NCAA spells one name differently (Ilia Snitari; Wikipedia has Ilya) and the file takes the NCAA's. Seeds 1 to 8 carry their seed; the eight players seeded 9-16 as a group all carry seed 9; everyone else is unseeded. A match's score is sets won; the women's Round of 16 walkover (Emily Welker over Lily Jones, injured) has no score. Each quarter of the draw is a region through the quarterfinals. Match times are on the printed brackets but not loaded. Neither source gives rankings or nationalities: the rankings are an ordering (seeds 1 to 8, then the 9-16 group as Wikipedia lists them by last name, then the rest in draw order), every player's country is the schools' (US), and the odds to win are made up in ranking order.
